subject: Business
title: Route Optimization: The Traveling Salesman Problem
description: A quick win: understand Route Optimization: The Traveling Salesman Problem.

hook.text: A delivery truck has 25 stops. The number of possible routes is 15 septillion. Computers find the best one in seconds.

buildup.text: Route optimization finds the shortest or cheapest path through multiple delivery points.

discovery.text: UPS saved 10 million gallons of fuel per year by eliminating left turns. Small route tweaks have massive impact.

twist.text: Perfect optimization is mathematically impossible for large numbers of stops. Algorithms find 'good enough' fast.

climax.text: UPS's ORION system analyzes 250,000 routing options per driver per day, saving $300-400 million annually.

punchline.text: The shortest distance between 25 points is a math problem worth billions.

quiz.question: How did UPS save 10 million gallons of fuel per year?
options: By optimizing routes to eliminate unnecessary left turns
By reducing the number of delivery stops

details.summary: Route optimization finds the most efficient path for delivery vehicles to visit multiple destinations, minimizing distance, time, or fuel cost. The underlying traveling salesman problem is one of the most studied challenges in mathematics and computer science.
details.whyItMatters: Fuel and driver time are major logistics costs. Route optimization algorithms reduce miles driven, cut delivery times, and lower carbon emissions. Even small percentage improvements across thousands of daily routes generate massive savings.
takeaways: The traveling salesman problem seeks the shortest route visiting all stops once
Heuristic algorithms find near-optimal solutions for practical route planning
GPS and real-time traffic data enable dynamic route adjustment

faq.question: Why is the traveling salesman problem so difficult to solve?
faq.answer: The number of possible routes grows factorially with stops. Ten stops have 3.6 million possible routes. Twenty stops have over two quintillion possibilities. No algorithm can guarantee the optimal solution in reasonable time for large problems; heuristics find near-optimal solutions.

faq.question: How does UPS approach route optimization?
faq.answer: UPS uses its ORION system, which evaluates thousands of route alternatives per driver daily using advanced algorithms. The system famously avoids left turns to reduce idle time and accidents. ORION saves UPS over 100 million miles and 10 million gallons of fuel annually.
